title: State Entropy Regularization for Robust Reinforcement Learning

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2 definitions of d_P^pi and rho_P^pi; all subsequent entropy duality results
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines d_P^pi(s) = sum_{t=0}^infty gamma^t Pr(s_t=s), without the usual (1-gamma) normalization. Thus sum_s d_P^pi(s)=1/(1-gamma), not 1, while d_P^pi is repeatedly called a probability distribution and H_S(d_P^pi) is evaluated using an entropy definition stated only for mu in Delta_S. The proofs then explicitly assume it is a probability vector: e.g., A.1 concludes lambda*=1 because 'softmax and d^pi are probability vectors,' and applies the entropy/LSE convex conjugacy for a probability vector. This invalidates Theorem 3.1, Table 1, and the later results unless d is redefined as normalized or every formula is rederived for the unnormalized occupancy.

predicted_errors.error_location: Theorem 3.1 and Table 1, 'Worst Case Reward' column
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Even if d^pi is repaired to be normalized, the stated worst-case reward is inconsistent with the stated uncertainty set and robust-return formula. For state entropy, the constraint is LSE((r^pi-tilde r^pi)/alpha) <= epsilon/alpha + log S. At the optimizer, Delta r^pi = r^pi-tilde r^pi must equal alpha log d^pi + epsilon + alpha log S (up to action-level nonuniqueness). Hence one valid statewise adversarial reward is tilde r(s,a)=r(s,a)-alpha log d^pi(s)-epsilon-alpha log S. The paper omits the -alpha log S term. Its displayed reward instead yields robust return E[r]+alpha H(d)-epsilon, whereas Eq. (5) and Table 1 state E[r]+alpha(H(d)-log S)-epsilon. The same missing normalization constants occur in the policy and state-action rows: they should include -alpha log A and -alpha log(SA), respectively.

The claimed kernel-uncertainty lower bound is not established by the proof. In Eq. (28), the Jensen/importance-sampling argument produces terms under the nominal occupancy rho_P^pi, including E_{rho_P^pi}[log tilde rho_P^pi]. But Eq. (31) abruptly replaces this with min_{tilde P} E_{rho_{tilde P}^pi}[log rho_{tilde P}^pi], a different expectation and a different function; no equality or inequality justifies this replacement. Eq. (33) then likewise replaces the fixed term E_{rho_P^pi}[log r] by min_{tilde P} E_{rho_{tilde P}^pi}[log r]. These changes do not follow from Eqs. (26)-(30). Moreover, the theorem statement gives no actual bound or formally defined kernel uncertainty set, only a narrative disclaimer, so it does not support the claimed result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A.4, Eq. (27), and Corollary A.2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The derivation takes log r(s,a) and exponentiates a bound involving E[log r], which requires strictly positive rewards. The main MDP definition allows arbitrary real rewards, and Corollary A.2 is stated for 'any' policy, alpha, and the displayed uncertainty set without a positivity assumption on r. Therefore the corollary is undefined for standard RL tasks with zero or negative rewards. Theorem 3.3 vaguely mentions restrictive positivity assumptions but does not state them mathematically, and the corollary omits them entirely.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.6, Eq. (41) and proof of Theorem 4.2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (41) is not the stated CVaR of the worst beta-fraction of returns. The expression min_eta {eta + (1/(1-beta)) E[(R-eta)^+]} is an upper-tail functional for returns (equivalently a common loss-CVaR form after a sign/convention change), not lower-tail/worst-outcome CVaR_beta as described in the text. The subsequent proof instead invokes a lower-tail dual set with density bound 1/beta. Thus the definition and the dual representation use incompatible tails and incompatible beta versus 1-beta conventions. The theorem's risk-averse conclusion consequently is not proved for the objective it defines.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, Section 5, and Appendix B.3 citations to [6] for PR-MDP/NR-MDP
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [6] is Chen et al. (2019), 'Top-K off-policy correction for a REINFORCE recommender system.' It is not the PR-MDP/NR-MDP robust-adversarial-control work. The paper calls '[6]' the source of 'the PR-MDP and NR-MDP frameworks' and labels its action-robust baselines '[6]'. The relevant cited work in this bibliography is instead Pinto et al. (2017), reference [47], 'Robust adversarial reinforcement learning.' This is a substantive misattribution of the baseline methodology.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 5, 'Sensitivity to rollout budget' and 'Regularization temperature' paragraphs versus Figure 5 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The rollout-budget paragraph says 'Figure 5(b) shows' the rollout effect, but Figure 5(b) is explicitly captioned 'Reward Shift'; the rollout-per-entropy-estimation ablation is Figure 5(c). Conversely, the temperature paragraph says the temperature sweep is in 'Figure 5(c),' but the caption identifies Figure 5(d) as 'Varying Regularization Strengths.' These are incorrect figure references for central experimental claims.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3 theoretical claims versus Appendix B.3-B.4 experimental implementation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The theory concerns entropy of the full MDP state-visitation distribution d_P^pi. However, the continuous-control experiments explicitly compute entropy only over a projection: in Pusher, 'the puck's x,y positions,' and in Ant, 'the height and orientations of the ant.' Entropy of a projection is generally not state entropy and need not have the reward-robust duality or kernel arguments claimed for H_S(d_P^pi). The experiments may study feature-entropy regularization, but they cannot be presented as empirical validation of the full-state theoretical guarantees without a projection-specific derivation.

References [25] and [26] are the same paper with identical authors and title, 'Accelerating reinforcement learning with value-conditional state entropy exploration.' They are listed once as NeurIPS 2023 and again as 'Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 36, 2024.' NeurIPS volume 36 corresponds to the 2023 proceedings, so the second entry is both a duplicate and incorrectly dated. Appendix B.2 specifically cites [26] as its code base, making the duplicated/incorrect reference consequential for reproducibility.
